children: Ampol's 3Q update surprised Jefferies for two opposing reasons. Ampol's Convenience Retail business continues to deliver despite weak consumer sentiment, high fuel prices and a tougher fuel margin backdrop. However, Jefferies's says the performance of Ampol's refining arm was weaker than expected. Ampol captured less of the upside from strong regional cracks, largely due to extended planned maintenance, Jefferies says. It retains a "hold" call and trims its price target by 3.3%, to A$44.00/share. "Convenience execution is creditable, Refining margin should be a tailwind for some time and FSSP 2 likely positive, but upside is largely priced in," analyst Michael Simotas says. FSSP 2 refers to the expected outcome of a review into the government's Fuel Security Services Payment, which supports refiners during times of low refining profitability. Ampol ended Monday at A$41.93. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
